common_name: Lemon Flare Japanese Laurel (Compact Yellow-Speckled Evergreen Shrub)

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring or early fall into humus-rich, well-drained soil in dappled to deep shade; a male Hawksridge Nursery selection valued for its densely gold-speckled foliage rather than for berries.

directions: Plant in a shaded bed protected from midday sun and drying winds, working compost into the backfill to hold moisture around the root ball. Foliage color develops most vividly on new spring growth, so light thinning of older stems each year keeps the shrub glowing. Water regularly through the first two seasons until established, then taper to occasional deep soaking during dry spells. Pair with ferns or hostas for a dependable gold accent in a woodland-style bed.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden
North Carolina State University Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Suruga Benten Japanese Laurel (Gold-Splashed Serrated-Leaf Evergreen Shrub)

planting.note: Install in part to full shade in fertile, well-drained soil; this Japanese female selection carries heavily serrated leaves washed in bright yellow around irregular green blotches, brightest on emerging cream-yellow new growth.

directions: Site out of direct afternoon sun, which can scorch the pale variegated leaf margins, and mulch to keep roots cool and evenly moist. A nearby male aucuba will improve berry set if fruit display is wanted, though this cultivar is prized mainly for its foliage contrast. Prune lightly in spring only to remove winter dieback or to shape, since flowering and variegation occur on older wood. Excellent as a specimen or informal hedge brightening a dim shade border.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

planting.note: Plant this larger female selection in humus-rich, moisture-retentive shade soil; new leaves emerge nearly creamy white each spring, aging to a striking contrast against the older dark green foliage, followed by red berries in fall.

directions: Give this vigorous, upright form room to reach full size, since crowding hides the seasonal show of pale new growth against mature dark leaves. Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged, especially during the spring flush when new foliage is expanding. Grow a male aucuba nearby to ensure the bright red autumn berries that make this cultivar stand out through winter. Underplant with shade groundcovers to hide bare lower stems as the shrub matures.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

common_name: Ooba Nakafu Japanese Laurel (Large Gold-Centered Evergreen Shrub)

planting.note: Set in dependable shade with rich, well-drained soil; this highly regarded Japanese selection bears large green leaves overlaid with a bold, stable yellow central blotch that holds its pattern better than many older variegated aucubas.

directions: Choose a shaded site with some protection from harsh winter sun, which can bleach the vivid central variegation on older leaves. Water deeply during establishment and in prolonged summer dry spells, then rely on natural rainfall once roots are settled. Because the gold pattern is unusually stable compared with other variegated forms, this cultivar makes a reliable long-term focal point rather than reverting to plain green. Combine with textured shade perennials to set off the bold leaf pattern.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

planting.note: Plant this little-known female Japanese selection in shaded, fertile, well-drained soil; leaves carry both fine yellow freckling and a broad central yellow pattern, giving a two-layered variegation effect distinct from more common aucubas.

directions: Grow in full to partial shade where the layered speckle-and-blotch variegation can be appreciated up close, such as along a shaded path or entry. Maintain even soil moisture through the first year or two, then reduce watering as the root system matures. Plant near a male aucuba if a berry display is desired, since this is a female clone. Because it remains uncommon in trade, source cuttings or plants only from reputable specialty growers to ensure correct identity.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

common_name: Wandering Sweet Box (Tall Large-Leaf Fragrant Evergreen Shrub)

planting.note: Site in full to part shade in humus-rich, evenly moist soil; this uncommon species (synonym S. balansae) has notably large leaves to 6 inches long and grows taller and more open than the compact hookeriana forms typically grown.

directions: Give this taller, larger-leaved sweet box a sheltered woodland-style position, since it suits mild-winter gardens better than the more cold-hardy Himalayan species. Keep soil consistently moist and enriched with leaf mold or compost, mimicking the humid understory conditions of its native range. Tiny inconspicuous flowers open in winter and spring and carry the characteristic sweet box fragrance despite their small size, so plant near a path or doorway where the scent can be enjoyed. Because it is still rare in cultivation, obtain plants from specialty or native-plant nurseries rather than general garden centers.
